description: I care about nature and sustainable practices, i enjoy finding about the local knowledge and wise advices of those who grow the land.
summary:
Mogen It a crop wizard tool powered by NASA POWER and open data, that helps growers analize their farm plot and be matched with suitable crops according the soil, humidity, altitude, NDVI with only 4 geo points in a map.

The tool assist the farmers through the different stages of ther crop with sat data and connect farmers through phenology observation based o their community knowledge base like early blooming and bird behaviours to be prepared for unexpected events.
details:
Climate no longer behaves the way it used to, and that affects the livelihood of farmers around the world. Mogen helps smallholder farmers in Chiloé, Chile, get ahead of the trend with data without requiring the technical knowledge to understand satellital data.

The farmer draws their plot on a map. The app retrieves its weather, soil and terrain, and measures its greenness with satellite images from NASA (HLS, 30 m) and ESA (Sentinel-2, 10 m). Weather comes from NASA POWER, CR2MET and Open-Meteo, and fires from NASA FIRMS.

We focused in actionable data for farmers that lack the professional assistance of Crop planning and data.

Plot map. The plot is divided into cells of about an acre, shown on a map with three layers: greenness, elevation and slope. The farmer can see which part of the field is greener and which part is steep or low for irrigation, instead of one average for the whole plot.

What to plant. Mogen ranks the species from a 2000+ database from FAO that suit the plot and estimates when each crop will flower and project the weather for the different stages. The farmer can rank crops with or without irrigation, and test a future climate scenario to prepare for the worst case.

Irrigation guide. For each crop, Mogen keeps a daily water balance of the root zone, using the plot’s rain and evaporation data. It says whether to irrigate today, the latest date to do it.

Alerts. The app checks the 16-day forecast against the stages when each crop is most vulnerable. It warns about frost, heat, humid spells that favor blight, and rain at harvest. It also flags fires detected by NASA satellites near the plot, with the crop’s stage on that day.

Community knowledge
Farmers can share local signs such as birds and flowering. When several different farmers in a zone report the same sign, it is shown with what the community says it announces, such as frost or a wet season. This is local knowledge, not validated against weather data, and it does not change the calculations. Crop stages the farmer confirms do adjust the estimated dates.


Data Sources:
It uses NASA data (POWER for weather and radiation, FIRMS for fire detections and HLS for greenness at 30 m), together with Sentinel-2 and Copernicus DEM from ESA, CR2MET weather and CLSoilMaps soils from the University of Chile’s CR2, SoilGrids from ISRIC, the Open-Meteo forecast, Chile’s Explorador Solar from the Ministry of Energy, crop requirements from FAO EcoCrop and ecoregions from RESOLVE.

Our stack is React, TypeScript, Vite and Leaflet, with a Python API (FastAPI) and a PostgreSQL database with PostGIS, deployed on Railway with a daily job that refreshes the data.
dataRefs: NASA POWER (clima diario y climatología: temperatura, lluvia, humedad, radiación solar)
NASA FIRMS (focos de calor VIIRS NOAA-20 y NOAA-21, casi en tiempo real)
NASA AppEEARS (extracción de datos por punto y área)
HLS Landsat 30 m, HLSL30 v2.0 (NDVI y otros índices ópticos, máscara de nubes Fmask)
Landsat 8 Collective 2 Surface Temperature, L08_ST v002 (temperatura de superficie)
NASA Earthdata (cuenta y acceso a los productos anteriores)
projectRefs: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (Sentinel-1 y Sentinel-2, ESA)
Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (elevación y pendiente, ESA, en AWS Open Data)
CLSoilMaps (agua disponible del suelo en Chile, CR2)
CR2MET (precipitación y temperatura de Chile, CR2)
Biomes and Ecoregions 2017 (RESOLVE, Dinerstein et al.)
